items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: We had an English boy, a violinist named Boucher

ctx.x: studied German in school. And he turned around to one of the dancers, Rufus Green to be exact, and grabbed Green by the coat. When he grabbed Green he clipped him on the chin and down he went. Now, he was so drunk he couldn't stand up. When Green hit him he went down and got up and shook himself and walked just as straight down Frederickstrasse as you've ever seen anybody right out of the crowd. That straightened him out. We found out in those days, you know, the Germans used to carry large canes. And a German is…

here. Why don't you get out?" "We don't have anything to do with that." So, they locked the door and Bobby Martin picked up his glass of beer to drink it and they dumped the glass of beer out of his hand. When they did that -- we had a fellow who was an ex-fighter, another dancer, Chick Horsey. George wasn't on the scene that night, he was out in the street somewhere. But Chick Horsey was even tougher than George. We had an English boy, a violinist named Boucher -- he weighed about 190, 6'2" -- there was Bobby…

happened, I was there. Three of us, and we're sitting in a bar and a fellow sitting right on the other side of the room -- everytime he'd smoke a cigarette butt down, he'd flip it over at us -- flip it over at our table. So, Sam Wooding's a funny guy. If he tells you he's going to hit you or he's going to shoot you, or what he's going to do, he'll do it. So, Sam just casually said, "If he flips another one of those cigarettes over here, I'm going to throw this glass at him -- I'll throw this ashtray at him." I…
